related.why: Examining the hernia this anatomy explains
Chronic groin pain as a specific risk

brief.scenario: This is a verbal applied anatomy viva on the right inguinal region of a male, with the external oblique aponeurosis opened. The examiner will describe structures by their position and relations, and ask you to name them.
brief.task: Name each structure the examiner describes and answer the examiner's questions on the anatomy of the inguinal canal and groin hernias.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: The canal is an oblique tunnel: deep ring laterally, superficial ring medially, the inferior epigastric vessels as the landmark between hernia types.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Confusing the midpoint of the inguinal ligament (deep ring) with the mid-inguinal point (femoral artery).
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: Anchor every answer to a landmark: "The deep ring lies just above the midpoint of the inguinal ligament."

grid.label: Rings and surface landmarks
grid.fail: Places the deep ring at the pubic tubercle, or mixes up the two landmarks.
grid.pass: Deep ring just above the midpoint of the inguinal ligament; superficial ring above and lateral to the pubic tubercle.
grid.high: Separates the midpoint of the inguinal ligament (deep ring) from the mid-inguinal point (femoral artery), and gives both bony references.

grid.label: Walls
grid.pass: Anterior: external oblique aponeurosis. Posterior: transversalis fascia. Roof: internal oblique and transversus. Floor: inguinal ligament.
grid.high: Adds reinforcements: internal oblique in front laterally, conjoint tendon behind medially, each strengthening the wall opposite a ring.

grid.label: Contents
grid.fail: Includes the femoral vessels, or omits the ilioinguinal nerve.
grid.pass: Spermatic cord (round ligament in women) and the ilioinguinal nerve.
grid.high: Lists cord contents: vas, three arteries, pampiniform plexus, genital branch of genitofemoral; ilioinguinal runs outside the cord.

grid.label: Coverings of the cord
grid.pass: External spermatic fascia, cremasteric fascia and muscle, internal spermatic fascia.
grid.high: Links each to its origin: external oblique, internal oblique, transversalis fascia.

grid.label: Direct versus indirect hernia
grid.fail: Says examination reliably tells direct from indirect.
grid.borderline: Knows indirect is lateral, but cannot name the vessels it is lateral to.
grid.pass: Indirect: through the deep ring, lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels. Direct: through Hesselbach's triangle, medial to them.
grid.high: Names the triangle's borders and states the distinction is confirmed at surgery, not reliably on examination.

grid.label: Inguinal versus femoral
grid.fail: Cannot place a femoral hernia relative to the pubic tubercle.
grid.pass: Inguinal hernias emerge above and medial to the pubic tubercle; femoral hernias below and lateral.
grid.high: Explains why femoral hernias strangulate more readily: a narrow, rigid neck with the lacunar ligament medially.

grid.label: Nerves at risk in repair
grid.fail: Cannot name a nerve at risk in open repair.
grid.pass: Names the ilioinguinal nerve as at risk, causing chronic groin pain or numbness.
grid.high: Knows the courses of the ilioinguinal, iliohypogastric and genital branch of genitofemoral nerves, and that recognising them at open repair reduces chronic pain.

grid.label: Handling uncertainty
grid.fail: Names a structure confidently and wrongly when unsure.
grid.pass: States uncertainty, then reasons from the described position and relations before naming.
grid.high: Gives a two-item differential with a reason, then commits.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Over the femoral pulse, at the mid-inguinal point.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What forms the walls of the canal?

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: A man has a groin hernia that you can control at the deep ring. Direct or indirect?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Indirect. You can always tell on examination.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Where does a femoral hernia sit?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'm not sure how it differs from an inguinal one.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: A nerve runs through the canal lying on the front of the cord, outside its coverings, and emerges through that opening. What is it?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It's definitely the genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: With the external oblique aponeurosis opened, there is an opening in the aponeurosis just above the pubic tubercle, with the cord passing out through it. What is it, and where is the other ring of the canal?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: That is the superficial ring, above and lateral to the pubic tubercle. The deep ring is just above the midpoint of the inguinal ligament.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Anterior, external oblique aponeurosis. Posterior, transversalis fascia. Roof, the arching fibres of internal oblique and transversus. Floor, the inguinal ligament.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The spermatic cord and the ilioinguinal nerve.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: External spermatic fascia, cremasteric fascia and muscle, and internal spermatic fascia.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Indirect hernias come through the deep ring, lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels. Direct hernias push through Hesselbach's triangle, medial to them.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Below and lateral to the pubic tubercle; inguinal hernias are above and medial.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What nerve are you careful of in an open repair?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The ilioinguinal nerve. Injury can cause chronic groin pain or numbness.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: A nerve runs through the canal lying on the front of the cord, outside its coverings, and emerges through that opening. What is it?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'm not certain. It lies on the front of the cord, outside it, and leaves through the superficial ring, so I think it's the ilioinguinal nerve.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: With the external oblique aponeurosis opened, there is an opening in the aponeurosis just above the pubic tubercle, with the cord passing out through it. What is it, and where is the other ring of the canal?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: That's the superficial ring, above and lateral to the pubic tubercle. The deep ring lies just above the midpoint of the inguinal ligament, halfway between the anterior superior iliac spine and the pubic tubercle. That's different from the mid-inguinal point, halfway to the pubic symphysis, where the femoral artery lies.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: External oblique in front, transversalis fascia behind, internal oblique and transversus as the roof, the inguinal ligament as the floor. Internal oblique reinforces the front laterally, over the deep ring, and the conjoint tendon reinforces the back medially, behind the superficial ring.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The cord: vas, testicular, cremasteric and vasal arteries, the pampiniform plexus, and the genital branch of genitofemoral. The ilioinguinal nerve runs in the canal but outside the cord.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: External spermatic from external oblique, cremasteric from internal oblique, internal spermatic from transversalis fascia.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Can you tell direct from indirect clinically?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Not reliably. Indirect is lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, direct is through Hesselbach's triangle: inferior epigastrics laterally, rectus medially, inguinal ligament below. The distinction is confirmed at surgery.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Below and lateral to the pubic tubercle. The neck is narrow and rigid, with the lacunar ligament medially, so it strangulates more readily.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Nerves in an open mesh repair?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The ilioinguinal, the iliohypogastric and the genital branch of genitofemoral. Knowing their courses and recognising them at surgery reduces the risk of chronic groin pain, because injury or entrapment causes it.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: A nerve runs through the canal lying on the front of the cord, outside its coverings, and emerges through that opening. What is it?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: It's either the ilioinguinal or the iliohypogastric. It runs on the front of the cord and exits the superficial ring, so it's the ilioinguinal.

failures.move: Putting the ilioinguinal nerve inside the spermatic cord.
failures.consequence: It runs outside the cord, which is why it is exposed during open repair.

failures.move: Listing the cord coverings without their origins.
failures.consequence: Misses the link to the abdominal wall layers, which is what the question tests.

failures.move: Not naming a nerve at risk in hernia repair.
failures.consequence: Misses the applied point: nerve injury causes chronic groin pain.

failures.move: Confusing the midpoint of the inguinal ligament with the mid-inguinal point.
failures.consequence: Places the deep ring over the femoral artery.

recovery.line: I can't identify that with certainty. From its position, I'd favour X over Y, because…

recovery.when: You mix up the two midpoints
recovery.line: Let me separate them: ASIS to pubic tubercle for the deep ring; ASIS to pubic symphysis for the femoral artery.

knowledge.fact: The canal runs about 4 cm, above the medial half of the inguinal ligament.
Deep ring: just above the midpoint of the inguinal ligament. Femoral artery: at the mid-inguinal point, halfway between ASIS and pubic symphysis.
Hesselbach's triangle: inferior epigastric vessels laterally, rectus abdominis medially, inguinal ligament inferiorly.
Cord coverings: external spermatic (external oblique), cremasteric (internal oblique), internal spermatic (transversalis fascia).
HerniaSurge (strong recommendation): nerve anatomy awareness and recognition during surgery reduce chronic post-herniorrhaphy pain. It does not require full dissection of each nerve.

recall.think: Which side of the inferior epigastric vessels, and which side of the pubic tubercle?
recall.say: "Deep ring above the midpoint of the ligament; femoral artery at the mid-inguinal point."
do: Name each described structure out loud
Hernia type by its relation to the landmarks

numbers.meaning: nerves to recognise in open mesh repair

recall.trap: Midpoint of the inguinal ligament ≠ mid-inguinal point.
recall.finish: Direct versus indirect is confirmed at surgery; protect the ilioinguinal nerve.

partner.opening: This is a verbal viva on the right inguinal region of a male, with the external oblique aponeurosis opened. I'll describe structures; name each one, then we'll discuss them.

reveals.finding: Read out: with the external oblique aponeurosis opened, there is an opening in the aponeurosis just above the pubic tubercle, with the cord passing out through it. Ask what it is and where the other ring lies.
Read out: a nerve runs through the canal lying on the front of the cord, outside its coverings, and emerges through that opening. Ask what it is.

reveals.trigger: After the rings and the nerve
reveals.finding: Read out: viewed from inside the abdomen, a pair of vessels arise from the external iliac vessels just above the inguinal ligament and run upwards and medially, immediately medial to the deep ring, towards the rectus sheath. Ask what they are and why they matter in groin hernias.

push.question: What are the walls of the canal?
push.expect: External oblique, transversalis fascia, internal oblique and transversus, inguinal ligament; the two reinforcements.

push.question: What does the cord contain, and what covers it?
push.expect: Vas, three arteries, pampiniform plexus, genital branch; three fascial coverings.

push.question: Where does a femoral hernia sit, and why does it strangulate?
push.expect: Below and lateral to the pubic tubercle; narrow rigid neck, lacunar ligament medially.

push.question: Which nerves are at risk in open repair?
push.expect: Ilioinguinal, iliohypogastric, genital branch of genitofemoral.

curveballs.prompt: You controlled it at the deep ring, so it must be indirect?
curveballs.safeAnswer: That suggests indirect, but clinical distinction is unreliable; it's confirmed at surgery.

curveballs.prompt: Where exactly is the mid-inguinal point?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Halfway between the ASIS and the pubic symphysis; the femoral artery lies there, not the deep ring.

curveballs.prompt: After his repair he has burning pain over the groin and scrotum. Why?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Likely injury or entrapment of the ilioinguinal nerve or genital branch of genitofemoral.
